reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 describes SPS of a high-entropy boride with SiC, not Si addition to ZrB2, and explicitly states no silicide phases formed because Si converted to SiC—contradicting the premise of a SiO2-rich intergranular film. E2 demonstrates liquid-phase sintering of a high-entropy boride composite using a eutectic liquid and formation of a ZrB12 intergranular phase, not a Si-based transient liquid or SiO2 film. Neither passage provides evidence for Si-induced densification, SiO2 formation, or improved oxidation/corrosion resistance in ZrB2.
premises: Si additive forms a transient liquid phase during SPS that enhances densification of ZrB2 at ~1600 °C
Post-sintering, Si segregates to grain boundaries and oxidizes to form a continuous, adherent SiO2-rich intergranular film
The SiO2-rich film significantly improves oxidation resistance and liquid metal corrosion durability
The Si-doped ZrB2 achieves mechanical strength comparable to conventional high-temperature sintered ZrB2
No deleterious silicide phases form if Si content and sintering parameters are precisely controlled
